title: Orlando City SC 1-3 FC Cincinnati: Evander at the double in Wild Card win
subtitle: FC Cincinnati sealed a date with Nashville SC in Round One of the MLS Cup playoffs, with Evander starring in their win over Orlando City SC.
paragraphs: FC Cincinnati came from a goal down to advance to the next round of the MLS Cup playoffs as Evander took centre stage in a 3-1 win over Orlando City SC at Inter.co Stadium.
Martin Ojeda had given Orlando a 26th-minute lead before two goals either side of half-time from Cincinnati captain Evander turned the Wild Card match on its head.
The win was sealed late on by Samuel Gidi, who was teed up by Evander, with a Round One best-of-three series with Supporters' Shield holders Nashville SC up next.
Orlando started brightly and took the lead through Ojeda. The Lions' skipper was slipped in behind by Ivan Angulo before taking a touch and finishing into the bottom-right corner.

However, Cincinnati hauled themselves level two minutes before the break when Evander sent Maxime Crepeau the wrong way from the penalty spot after Pavel Bucha was fouled inside the area by Marco Pasalic.
Evander was it again in the 49th minute to put Orlando ahead, turning in from close range on the rebound after Tom Barlow's initial effort was saved but fell kindly back to him.
Orlando almost restored parity when Ojeda's goal-bound strike looked certain to ripple the net, but with Roman Celentano beaten, Gidi was on hand to clear the ball off the line.
And it was Gidi who ensured the victory in some style. After collecting Evander's pass out on the left, he cut inside and bent a glorious shot past Crepeau in the 85th minute.
In the Western Conference Wild Card match, Real Salt Lake beat the Seattle Sounders 4-2 on penalties to book their place in Round One following a 1-1 draw in normal time.

Albert Rusnak opened the scoring in the 36th minute, five minutes after seeing his penalty saved by Rafael Cabral, but RSL levelled through Morgan Guilavogui just after the hour, though neither side was able to find a winner.
Dejan Joveljic and Rusnak's spot-kicks were saved in the shoot-out to hand RSL the advantage, with Sergi Solans and Lukas Engel both converting from 12 yards out.
Paul Rothrock got Seattle on the board, but it was too little too late as RSL stayed perfect, with Philip Quinton sealing a best-of-three series with the Vancouver Whitecaps.
Evander ends Cincinnati's away day play-off woes

Cincinnati may have felt the odds were stacked against them in their first match of the postseason. They were without a win in their last four away playoff matches (D1 L3) ahead of facing Orlando, but their Brazilian magician led them to victory.

Indeed, it was Cincinnati's first playoff win on the road since their first ever game in the postseason as an MLS team back in 2022 against the New York Red Bulls, and Evander led from the front to seal a date with Nashville.

Evander now has 16 goals for the season with Cincinnati, only one fewer than Kevin Denkey for Pat Noonan's side, while he also finished with team-high totals for shots on target (three), chances created (three), touches (67) and passes in the final third (29).

But Orlando had more than enough chances to at least force penalties. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.91 from their 27 attempts compared to Cincinnati's 1.65 from their 10 shots, with the Lions left to rue a glut of missed opportunities as their campaign came to an end.
